title: Introduce shadow traffic and per-tenant degradation budgets to address tail-latency autoscale incident
creator: Asha Menon
description: Translate postmortem action items from the 2026-01-29 autoscale tail-latency incident into concrete PRD updates and acceptance criteria. Deliverables: (1) a specification for a "synthetic tenant shadowing" harness that replays production-like traffic to candidate runtime changes without affecting serving tenants, (2) per-tenant degradation budget model and UI in Console, and (3) rollout gating rules that require shadow verification and budget compliance before production rollout.
background: On 2026-01-29 we observed tail-latency spikes during an autoscale event affecting a subset of tenants with large KV cache footprints. Postmortem identified regression risk when kernel scheduling and cache rehydration interact under burst scale-up. Current PRDs lack explicit verification steps that exercise multi-tenant cold-start and cache-regen behavior in a safe, production-like way. Engineering and SRE recommended two primary mitigations: implement shadow traffic verification for candidate deployments, and limit per-tenant degraded request budgets to prevent noisy neighbors from causing cluster-level escalations.
acceptance_criteria: PRD contains end-to-end spec for synthetic tenant shadowing including traffic composition, latency and token distribution targets, and isolation guarantees
Shadow harness implemented in staging and linked to CI so every runtime release executes a shadow verification job prior to canary rollout
Console UI mockups and API defined for per-tenant degradation budgets and visible budget burn-down metrics
Rollout gating rules added: a release cannot advance to canary unless shadow verification passes and per-tenant budget estimates indicate < 2% expected degradation for targeted tenants
Runbook updated: clear playbook for failing shadow verifications with rollback criteria and operator steps
Automated synthetic test that reproduces the original incident class runs in CI and demonstrates the protection (tail-latency stays within SLOs under scaled KV cache churn)
success_metrics: Reduce recurrence probability of autoscale-induced tail-latency regressions by >90% for addressed root cause class
Number of releases blocked by shadow verification failures that would have otherwise caused degraded customer latency: tracked and reviewed quarterly
Mean time to detect degradation in pre-production (shadow) < 15 minutes
Per-tenant degradation budget violated < 0.5% of tenants per quarter

Design Console UX: per-tenant degradation budget editor and budget burn charts (owner: Design)
Implement shadow traffic harness in infra: controller to mirror sampled production traffic to isolated harness clusters (owner: ENG)
Add CI step: run shadow verification job against candidate runtime artifacts (owner: ENG)
Define rollout gates: update release automation to require shadow verification pass and budget sanity check (owner: ENG/Platform)
Create synthetic replay dataset and load test that reproduces incident characteristics (owner: SRE/Research)
Update runbooks and incident playbooks to include shadow verification triage steps (owner: SRE)
Document design and runbook links in PRD and Console help (owner: PM/DevRel)
progress_updates: 2026-02-11: Scoping workshop with SRE, runtime, and Console teams. Aligned on shadowing concept and budget model.
2026-02-18: Engineering prototype of a lightweight shadow controller completed. Initial results show no impact to production paths when sampling <=1% of traffic.
2026-02-26: Design shared console mockups for budget editor; PM feedback requested on terminology and defaults.
2026-03-05: SRE produced a synthetic replay dataset that reproduces KV cache regen tail latency in staging. Next: integrate into CI.
2026-03-12: Raised dependency ENG-91222 for canary gate automation. Meeting scheduled to finalize automation contract.
risks: Shadow traffic at production fidelity may leak PII if not properly sanitized — requires review with Security and Privacy
Sampling too low may not catch regression; sampling too high may increase CI cost and slow pipelines
Operator complexity: adding per-tenant budgets increases surface area for support and potential misconfiguration
False positives in shadow verification could block safe releases; need robust signal and tolerances
mitigations: Work with Security to define sanitization pipeline and certs before sampling production traffic
Prototype sampling thresholds and run calibration round to find the cost/coverage sweet spot
Provide sane defaults for budgets and guardrails in Console; add role-based permissions for editing budgets
Build a two-stage verification: automated pass/fail plus a short human review for borderline failures
qa_plan: Create CI job that runs the synthetic replay and shadow harness in a pre-production cluster for each candidate runtime build. Define pass conditions (95th percentile latency < SLO threshold; error rate increase < 0.1%). Add flaky-run detection and retest policy. Include an e2e test that exercises Console budget changes and verifies enforcement via simulated tenant requests.
